content:
sam: Quick follow-up from the RFC review — we need a concrete proposal for flow-control signals across the gateway and how they interact with idempotent retry boundaries for streaming requests. Thinking about partial responses, client-side progress, and safe midstream fallbacks.

ravi: +1. Do you mean a wire-level marker or something carried in the application headers/state? :thinking_face:

sam: Wire-level but visible to the gateway runtime. Two concerns: 1) let clients know how far the model progressed (for UX / partial renders) and 2) let us know a safe cut point for retrying vs resuming vs falling back.

maria: Can we sketch a minimal header set? I worry about exposing internal token indices to clients (privacy/implementation leaking). Maybe opaque checkpoints instead.

ravi: Proposal sketch: headers and trailers we can use between client <-> frontdoor <-> worker. Example:

```
X-Stream-Checkpoint: v1;ckpt=base64(payload);offset=1024
X-Stream-Progress: 42/200
X-Idempotency-Key: <client-generated>
X-Handoff-Intent: resume|restart|nop
```

- ckpt is opaque to clients if we want; gateway only needs to understand a canonical serialization.

kevin: We should be explicit about semantics:
- resume: worker has checkpoint and can resume generation without re-executing prefix
- restart: start from scratch (useful for non-resumable backends)
- nop: no preference (gateway chooses)

sam: Right. Tradeoffs: storing checkpoints at the gateway vs carrying them to the worker. Storing at gateway -> memory pressure & TTLs. Carrying -> larger wire & client trust. Thoughts on TTLs and eviction policy?

maria: TTL should be short (~30s–2m) for low-latency interactive flows. For batch or long polls, we rely on persistent storage behind the gateway (dedicated checkpoint service) and a short lease at the gateway to accelerate resume. Evict LRU or size-based with per-tenant caps.

ravi: Also need to codify idempotency boundary: if checkpoint present and verified, we treat retry as safe for side-effect-free requests. If no checkpoint, fallback rules: either restart (best-effort) or proxy to a lower-cost model variant before failing.

kevin: Observability: emit metrics per-checkpoint: created, resumed, expired, resume-failure. Add trace span tags for checkpoint_id and resume_outcome. This lets us measure cost vs benefit.

infra-bot: RFC doc updated: https://internal.rw/infradocs/stream-checkpoints-v1 — diff added (sam, ravi)

maria: Edge-case: multi-tenant workers that dedupe similar requests — checkpoint serialization must include model version + config hash + route id to avoid accidental cross-request resumes. Include fields in ckpt payload: model, quant, prompt-hash, route.

sam: Good call. Also consider security: CKPT must be HMACed by our control plane key so frontdoor can verify authenticity if clients echo it back. Otherwise a malicious client could craft a fake ckpt to trick resumed tokens.

ravi: Implementation plan: 1) add header parsing to frontdoor (fast path ignored if absent), 2) small in-memory checkpoint cache with tenant caps + optional Redis backing, 3) worker API to accept resume token blob and return resume-accepted|resume-refused, 4) fallback workflow config (restart|fallback-model|fail).

kevin: Perf note: keep checkpoint blobs small — ideally <= 2KB. If larger, gateway should store and expose a short opaque id instead of inlining.

maria: UX: clients can opt-in to progress markers via a feature flag so we don't break current thin clients. Also document semantics: progress numbers are best-effort, not exact when retries happen.

sam: Action items: sam -> draft PR for frontdoor header + HMAC verification; ravi -> sketch checkpoint cache shim + quota; kevin -> metrics spans + perf budget; maria -> update RFC with security/ttl/serialization. I'll compile and post a follow-up RFC note in the doc linked by infra-bot. :thumbsup:

ravi: Sounds good. One more Q: do we gate resume to enterprise customers only? That affects cache size and TTL.

sam: Let's default to enabled for hosted and dedicated, off for private unless they opt-in (because of HSM/KMS differences). We'll call it out in the rollout plan.

kevin: +1 from me. I'll add a simple SLO test to ensure resuming doesn't regress p99 latency beyond threshold.

maria: Thanks — leaving a few inline comments in the RFC.

sam: Great thread. We'll sync in tomorrow's arch sync if anything contentious remains.
